title: Why Your Brain Gets Songs Stuck in It
sources: Involuntary musical imagery (earworms): roughly 90% of people experience them at least weekly (Liikkanen 2012; Beaman & Williams 2010)
Earworms are tied to the auditory cortex replaying recent music; catchy, repetitive, simple tunes are the stickiest (Jakubowski et al. 2017)
Active distraction and engaging tasks reduce earworm frequency; trying to suppress them can backfire (Beaman & Williams 2010)

lines.text: Why do songs get stuck in your head?
lines.caps: WHY DO *SONGS | GET STUCK | IN YOUR *HEAD?

lines.text: You're just living your life, minding your own business.
And suddenly a song from 2010 starts playing on loop.
Scientists call it involuntary musical imagery.
Your brain loves patterns, and songs are full of them.
Catchy hooks tickle that spot and refuse to leave.
The more you hear it, the deeper it digs in.
lines.caps: THE MORE YOU *HEAR IT | THE DEEPER IT *DIGS

lines.text: Even after the music stops, your brain keeps replaying it.
lines.caps: EVEN AFTER IT *STOPS | YOUR BRAIN *REPLAYS IT

lines.text: That's why it follows you right into the shower.
Trying to force it out only makes it stronger.
lines.caps: TRYING TO *PUSH IT OUT | MAKES IT *STRONGER

lines.text: But here's the trick: give your brain another song.
Or solve a little puzzle, and it usually wanders off.
So next time a tune hijacks your head, just ride it out.
lines.caps: NEXT TIME A *TUNE | HIJACKS YOUR HEAD | JUST *RIDE IT OUT
